findings.F1: On every bar where a coin is below its close of 30 days ago, a day that rose by 0.5 to 1.5 of its usual daily swing is followed by a next-day excess return (over the coin's drift) of -0.67 % (t -2.42, 266 days). A fall of more than 1.5 swings is followed by +1.07 % (t 1.81, 81 days). Across the down-30-day bars, today's scaled return times tomorrow's excess, summed per day, has a t of -1.96 (760 days), so a falling coin's up days are given back the next day.
findings.F2: Among the up days of coins that are down over 30 days, a deeper 30-day fall gives a larger next-day fall. By depth tercile the next-day excess is -1.03 % for the deepest (t -2.73, 181 days), -0.78 % for the middle (t -2.47, 241 days) and -0.20 % for the shallowest (t -0.84, 278 days). At about five times the 0.19 % cost of a trade, the deepest move is large enough to pay.
findings.F3: The give-back of up days in falling coins holds on all six coins: next-day excess from -0.34 % (LTC) to -1.12 % (ETH), with t from -0.74 to -2.39. It holds in three of the four years (2018 -1.12 % t -2.05, 2019 -0.62 %, 2020 -0.66 %; 2021 +0.36 %) and in 8 of the 12 windows.
findings.F4: The effect is not specific to the calm profile. Inside the falling calm profile, up days of 0.5 to 1.5 swings are followed by -0.31 % (t -0.87, 160 days). On down-30-day bars outside the profile they are followed by -0.84 % (t -2.66, 183 days).
findings.F5: The tested idea's grading is weak. Inside the profile, the next-day excess is -0.53 % for the deepest 30-day third (t -1.90), -0.51 % for the middle (t -2.10) and -0.24 % for the shallowest (t -0.88). Next day overall the profile earns -0.25 % excess (t -1.51, 647 days), and the idea's size is +0.13 % with t 0.51. Depth alone does not carry the continuation; F1 and F2 point instead to the up days inside the fall.
findings.F6: The crossing of 30-day and 1-day quintiles agrees. Coins in the second-lowest 30-day quintile with a top-quintile day fall -1.16 % the next day (t -3.22, 99 days). Coins in the lowest 30-day quintile with a fourth-quintile day fall -1.44 % (t -2.54, 128 days). The lowest 30-day quintile with a bottom-quintile day rebounds +0.97 % (t 2.01). Falls after falls rebound, a pattern the map already holds in its agitated rebound ideas; rises after falls are given back, which the map does not hold.
findings.F7: Over two days, up days of 0.5 to 1.5 swings in down-30-day coins are followed by -1.00 % excess (t -1.85, 142 days). The give-back is concentrated in the first day.

ideas.idea: When a coin that has fallen over the past 30 days closes a day higher, the deeper its 30-day fall, the more it falls over the next day, as holders who bought higher sell into the bounce.
ideas.consequence: A trader should treat an up day in a deep 30-day decline as a selling opportunity for the next day, more so the deeper the decline, and should not buy it as a turn.
ideas.name: falling coin bounce sold
